title: Capacity Lease Fallback Contract and Surge Arbitration PRD
creator: Maya Patel
description: PRD for a capacity-lease fallback contract and surge arbitration system to ensure tenants with reserved pools get graceful, predictable behavior when reserved capacity is constrained and to provide a controlled fallback path to on-demand or lower-cost model variants.
problem_statement: Reserved capacity customers occasionally experience transient capacity shortfalls due to regional outages, scheduling churn, and hot node loss. Current behavior either blocks requests (failed provisioning) or falls back in unpredictable ways that violate latency SLOs and customer expectations. We need a deterministic fallback contract and arbitration rules so applications can remain available with predictable degradation and cost implications.
goals: Define a lease-level fallback handshake: soft-fallback -> surge-credit -> preemptive-eviction -> on-demand routing
Expose tenant-configurable policies for grace windows, headroom targets, and allowable model variants during fallback
Implement arbiter service that makes per-request routing decisions consistent with tenant contract and global fairness
Provide telemetry and billing labels that explain fallback events and cost impact to customers and SREs
Ship APIs and console controls for tenants to opt into automatic fallback or strict enforcement
non_goals: Replacing existing long-term reservation pricing models
Full rewrite of scheduler; this will integrate with current allocator and preemption hooks
Automatic model quality adaptation (LLM outputs are expected to vary; quality monitoring is separate)
success_metrics: Reserved-tenant request success rate during 99th-percentile transient load improves from baseline by >= 40%
Median 95th-percentile latency regression during fallback < 2x baseline for allowed-on-demand fallbacks
Customer-facing incidents due to reserved pool exhaustion reduced by 80% in first 90 days
Number of tenants that opt-in to automatic fallback via Console > 40% of current eligible tenants within 60 days
user_stories: As a Platform engineer, I want a deterministic fallback policy per-lease so I can guarantee client apps how requests will be treated when reserved capacity is low
As an SRE, I want granular telemetry that attributes requests to fallback reasons (eviction, preemption, scheduler lag) so I can troubleshoot hotspots
As a Tenant admin, I want to configure a 60s grace window and allow fallbacks to a quantized model variant to reduce degraded output quality but keep latency stable
As Billing, I want all fallback events labeled for billing reconciliation so customers can see cost differences when on-demand was used
requirements: API: allow lease-level policy fields: grace_window_seconds, headroom_percent, allow_on_demand(boolean), max_fallback_model_tier(list of tier IDs), surge_credit_pool_id(optional)
Arbiter: implement per-lease decisioning service that returns: route(target_pool), cost_label, fallback_reason, estimated_latency_ms
Scheduler hooks: preemption-safe handoff that keeps KV caches for 30s when possible and marks evicted requests for preferential rewarm
Console: UI panels to edit fallback policy and a toggle for automatic vs strict enforcement
Telemetry: new metrics and traces: fallback_count, fallback_latency_impact, fallback_cost_delta, lease_headroom_seconds
Billing: tagging in billing events when on-demand compute is used for reserved lease requests
acceptance_criteria: Given a lease with allow_on_demand=true and headroom_percent=10, when reserved pool utilization exceeds 100% and no prewarm nodes available, the arbiter routes 80% of new requests to the preconfigured on-demand pool and leaves 20% queued until grace_window elapses

Given allow_on_demand=false and grace_window=30s, requests arriving after the grace window are rejected with HTTP 429 and response JSON includes fallback_reason: 'LEASE_EXHAUSTED' and suggested action: 'retry-after' header
Console shows per-lease fallback events with timestamp, fallback_reason, cost_delta, and affected request IDs for the last 7 days
Telemetry surfaces a new dashboard tile showing fallback_count and fallback_cost_delta per-tenant; dashboard query returns results within 2s for 30-day range
Billing events include 'fallback_cost_label' and reconcile to on-demand charges in billing export schema
Automated integration tests simulate node-loss and confirm the arbiter decisions follow policy and that KV cache continuity is preserved where scheduler supports it
Runbook created and validated by oncall with at least one playbook drill that simulates reserve exhaustion and verifies rollback paths
rollout_plan: Phase 1: feature-flagged backend + API + minimal Console controls to 10 internal tenants (4 weeks). Phase 2: enable for 100 beta customers with telemetry and billing labels (4 weeks). Phase 3: GA for all reserved leases with opt-in default set to allow_on_demand=false; education email + admin notification (2 weeks). Feature flags: arbiter-v1, fallback-console-ui, billing-fallback-tags.
telemetry_and_dashboards: New metrics will be ingested into metrics pipeline under names: redwood.lease.fallback.count, redwood.lease.fallback.latency_ms, redwood.lease.fallback.cost_delta. Create console dashboard: 'Lease Fallbacks' with breakdown by region, lease_id, and model_tier. Add logs: 'fallback_decision' structured log with fields [lease_id, decision, reason, request_id, estimated_latency_ms].
dependencies: ENG-allocator-team: scheduler preemption hooks and KV cache preservation (ENG-30922)
ENG-billing-team: add fallback_cost_label to billing export schema (ENG-31740)
Console: UI control surface and notifications (DES-21011)
Legal: update terms for on-demand billing during fallbacks (LEGAL-77)
open_questions: What default values should we ship for headroom_percent and grace_window? (suggest 10% and 30s)
How to prioritize fairness across multiple reserved tenants in the same zone when on-demand capacity is limited?
Should surge credits be transferable across regions or strictly zonal?
What SLA wording is appropriate for tenant opting into allow_on_demand=true?
notes_and_tradeoffs: We prioritize predictable behavior over absolute availability for strict tenants. Allowing on-demand fallback reduces outage incidents but can increase unit cost and impact output quality. We will document recommended defaults and surface cost previews in the Console. To reduce product complexity, regional cross-bindings of surge-credit pools will be out of scope for phase 1.
implementation_tasks: Scheduler: add preemption-safe KV preservation flag (ENG-allocator)
Billing: add labels and update exports (Nina)
Console: minimal policy editor and telemetry panels (Design + Frontend)
E2E tests: simulated node loss + correctness checks (QA)
QA_test_plan: Unit tests for arbiter decision matrix with permutations of headroom, grace_window, and allow_on_demand
Integration test that simulates scheduler node loss and verifies fallback_count and KV cache preservation
Load test: verify 95th-percentile latency impact under fallback with 1k qps burst
Billing test: verify fallback_cost_label appears in exported CSV and reconciles to raw billing entries
Console validation: policy edits save correctly and historic fallback events display with correct metadata
rollout_dates: Feature flag rollout to internal tenants starting 2025-03-31; beta ramp 2025-04-28; GA 2025-05-12
final_notes: PM will coordinate with SRE to run a live drill with three tenant types: strict, soft-fallback, and opt-in on-demand to validate metrics and customer messaging. Post-launch, run a 30-day evaluation and propose default policy changes based on observed customer behavior.
